pull.title: M3: daily digest and the rest of the CLI
pull.body:
Fourth milestone. IssueRadar now sends me a daily digest, so I don't have to remember to open anything.

What I did:

- Built the digest. It has the top free issues for me, my pull requests (filled in once the PR tracker lands in M4), free issues that are new since yesterday, alerts about watched repos (archived, gone quiet, or failing to sync), and a short note on quiet days.
- Made it remember what it already sent. An issue only comes back if something I'd notice changed, like its status or level. Running `firstpr digest --send` twice sends nothing the second time, and there's a test for exactly that.
- Added `firstpr dismiss` (never show it again) and `firstpr snooze --days 7`.
- Added delivery channels. Markdown files and an RSS feed work out of the box. Email, Telegram, Discord and Slack are there too, off until I switch them on, and their passwords and webhooks come from environment variables, not the config file. The delivery code refuses to send anything to a GitHub address.
- Added `firstpr init` (creates the config and skills files to edit), `firstpr export` (JSON dump), and a short "before you start" checklist at the end of `firstpr explain`.

Something I fixed along the way:

- The first version took 9.5 seconds to build a digest from 5,000 issues, which missed my 5-second target. Each issue was hitting the database separately, and every phrase check ran its own regex. After fixing both it takes about 2 seconds. The numbers and the command are in `RESULTS.md` (the 5,000 issues are generated, so it only measures speed).

To try it:

```powershell
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
firstpr init
firstpr sync
firstpr digest
firstpr digest --send
firstpr digest --send
```

The second `--send` should say there's nothing new. Setting up the other channels is in `docs/digest.md`.

timeline.message:
Make ranking about five times faster

Load PRs and signals once per run instead of once per issue, compile each
phrase list into one pattern, and check the language on a sample of the
text. A digest over 5,000 generated issues went from 9.5 s to about 2 s.
